beats.text: Six psychology facts that quietly explain your everyday life.
One. The mere-exposure effect: we start to like things, and people, simply because they're familiar.
Two. The spotlight effect: nobody notices your stumbles and flaws nearly as much as you do.
Three. Loss aversion: losing ten pounds stings more than finding ten pounds ever feels good.
Four. The Zeigarnik effect: unfinished tasks keep nagging the mind until they're closed.
Five. Emotional contagion: you quietly catch the moods of the people you spend time with.
Six. The peak-end rule: we judge an experience by its most intense moment and its ending — not its average.
Your mind runs on shortcuts. See them clearly, and you get a little harder to fool.
